**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Since we allow running subsets of controllers with --controllers, different subset controllers cannot run with leader election at the same time. The reason of that is election object name conflict.
So we want to add options for clients to customize the name and namespace of election object.

issue_context.title: Add resourceLockName options to leader election
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:
Add a options to set resource-lock-name for leader election
**Why is this needed**:
Think about this scenario: we want to split some controllers out of controller manager and deploy it isolated. It also needs leader election for ha. But now they will use the same resource-lock-name, we need to set it to a different from kube-controller-manager.
And it is the same issue for scheduler.
comments: what's the point of separating locks? or rather, which controller are you trying to separate from KCM? i presume separating controllers into multiple processes can lead to cache inconsistency, b/c in a single KCM process all controllers are reading from the same cache per resource. i noticed in scheduler, overriding lock name is already supported by #42961. @liggitt for thoughts
We deploy job/cronjob/daemonset controller out of KCM. Because our cluster scale is too large and KCM is often overloaded. I don't think it's a big risk if they have inconsistent cache.

We are proposing a _very_ similar thing here https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/979 but it's specifically for the cloud provider migration case. It should be extendable to other use-cases but needs a bit more consideration there. PTAL

> i noticed in scheduler, overriding lock name is already supported by #42961. @liggitt for thoughts

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/leaderelection/resourcelock/interface.go#L93-L94 already supports choosing a lock name. scheduler plumbs a flag to that. {kube,cloud}-controller-manager currently don't.

> i presume separating controllers into multiple processes can lead to cache inconsistency, b/c in a single KCM process all controllers are reading from the same cache per resource.

controller loops run asynchronously and independently. running them in separate processes would not be as efficient, but should not cause consistency issues.

> https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/leaderelection/resourcelock/interface.go#L93-L94 already supports choosing a lock name. scheduler plumbs a flag to that. {kube,cloud}-controller-manager currently don't.

Do you think this flag make sense for CM?

> controller loops run asynchronously and independently. running them in separate processes would not be as efficient, but should not cause consistency issues.

I understand they run independently. Running them in separate processes can isolated the cpu and memory resource.

> Do you think this flag make sense for CM?

since we allow running subsets of controllers with `--controllers`, probably so
@ricky1993 I'm curious how exactly you are setting the `--controllers` flags, cause in some scenarios if we add new controllers in `kube-controller-manager` you could miss it.
@andrewsykim We set --controllers=*,-foo,-bar at main kcm. And --controllers=foo,bar at the seperated kcms. I think it would not miss new controllers because * is a wildcard to match it.

review_comments: keep defaulting setting the LockObjectNamespace field. we want the files we generate to work for n-1 schedulers that only read that field

sorry, I meant *instead of* the new field. Defaulting both means `kube-scheduler --write-config-to=config.yaml` would write a file with both fields populated, which is pretty confusing. Same comment for LockObjectName

adding these fields (and corresponding flags) makes the scheduler configuration (which has its own lockObjectName/Namespace fields already) ambiguous. As part of adding these, we have to resolve that ambiguity in the scheduler config.

We could do the following in the scheduler config:
1. change the scheduler [lock-object-name/namespace flags to bind to the new struct fields](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cmd/kube-scheduler/app/options/deprecated.go#L61-L62), mark the flags as deprecated in favor of the new flags
2. remove the [LockObjectName/LockObjectNamespace fields from the internal scheduler configuration type](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/apis/config/types.go#L141-L144) (leave the fields in the external configuration type for compatibility)
3. mark the [LockObjectName/LockObjectNamespace fields in the external scheduler configuration type](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-scheduler/config/v1alpha1/types.go#L137-L140) as deprecated in favor of the new standard fields
4. modify the [scheduler configuration defaulting](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/apis/config/v1alpha1/defaults.go#L81-L86) to only default the LockObjectName/LockObjectNamespace fields if the new fields are not set
5. modify the [scheduler configuration conversion](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/apis/config/v1alpha1/zz_generated.conversion.go#L198-L224) to implement custom conversion methods to do the following:
    * Convert_v1alpha1_KubeSchedulerConfiguration_To_config_KubeSchedulerConfiguration
      * call autoConvert_v1alpha1_KubeSchedulerConfiguration_To_config_KubeSchedulerConfiguration, then:
      * If only one of LockObjectName/ResourceName is set (or if they are both set and match), copy that to internal ResourceName
      * If only one of LockObjectNamespace/ResourceNamespace is set (or if they are both set and match), copy that to internal ResourceNamespace
      * If old/new fields are both set and do not match, error
    * Convert_config_KubeSchedulerConfiguration_To_v1alpha1_KubeSchedulerConfiguration:
      * call autoConvert_config_KubeSchedulerConfiguration_To_v1alpha1_KubeSchedulerConfiguration, then:
      * Copy internal ResourceName to external LockObjectName and ResourceName
      * Copy internal ResourceNamespace to external LockObjectNamespace and ResourceNamespace
I expected these to be defaulted in config defaulting, not in Run()
That makes the default values appear in flag help
Sounds good. Shoud we migrate scheduler's option to here for consistent?

I am pretty nervous about offering these options.
1) it's now fairly easy to misconfigure and end up with multiple active controllers, which could be catastrophic (imagine thrashing over load balancers, for example)
2) is it possible to change these flags one replica at a time in a HA configuration? How?

> 1. it's now fairly easy to misconfigure and end up with multiple active controllers, which could be catastrophic (imagine thrashing over load balancers, for example)

In most case, we needn't configure these options. We will configure them when we want to seperate some controllers out of kcm.
> 2. is it possible to change these flags one replica at a time in a HA configuration? How?

I don't understand why we want to change these flags for a inflight controller.
If we want to do it, firstly stop the standby kcms, change all kcm's flags, restart the active kcm, restart the standby kcms.

The scheduler provides these flags before, it's designed for multi-scheduler, clients will only configure these flags for the new scheduler, but not to the inflight scheduler.
And now we just let kcm has the same ability.

Might be worth looking at https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/979. Stopping standby KCMs can be problematic as component status (CS) is always the local KCM. So it will make the KAS appear unhealthy via CS requests. Depending on the users/CPs monitoring system that may cause problems. More importantly the set of safe mechanisms for migrating from 1 CM to multiple CMs is not documented anywhere.

> Might be worth looking at [kubernetes/enhancements#979](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/979). Stopping standby KCMs can be problematic as component status (CS) is always the local KCM. So it will make the KAS appear unhealthy via CS requests. Depending on the users/CPs monitoring system that may cause problems. 

I think we'd better not to change leader election object in arbitrary for a inflight component. BTW these options are required for migrating multiple CMs.
> More importantly the set of safe mechanisms for migrating from 1 CM to multiple CMs is not documented anywhere.

I am glad to add a document about it in the next PR, and where should I put the document?

If we switch the resourceLock from endpoints to configmaps for a inflight CM, I think it is the same situation. It should be a new topic for migration lock of inflight CM. This PR doesn't add risk for clients.
